0.0.n: さん makes this a polite way to address the audience.

0.2.n: This standard evening greeting ends with は, pronounced わ.

1.1.n: This adjective describes the Japanese used in the program named here.

1.2.n: 日本語 refers to the language, not the country.

1.3.n: This borrowed word forms part of the program title.

1.4.n: This is part of the program name and echoes わん, a dog's bark.

1.6.n: の links the program title to 時間, identifying which program it is time for.

1.7.n: With a program title plus の, 時間 announces that the program is starting.

1.8.n: です gives the announcement a polite ending.

2.0.n: The speaker politely addresses the whole audience with さん.

2.2.n: The polite prefix お softens 久しぶり, a greeting used after time apart.

2.3.n: です makes the greeting polite; the sense of elapsed time comes from お久しぶり.

3.0.n: この must come before a noun; here it points to the current news program.

3.1.n: Here ニュース refers to the news presentation the speaker is introducing.

3.2.n: は marks このニュース as the topic, which the following lines explain.

3.3.n: This is the name of Japan's public broadcaster and part of the website name.

3.5.n: This English word is part of the website name NHK Web Easy.

3.7.n: This English word belongs to the website name, rather than functioning as a Japanese adjective.

3.8.n: など presents NHK Web Easy as one example, not the only source.

3.9.n: の connects the listed example sites to ニュースのホームページ later in the sentence.

4.0.n: 易しい describes 日本語 and is the kanji spelling of やさしい used earlier.

4.1.n: Here 日本語 names the language used to write the news.

4.2.n: で marks the language used for writing.

4.3.n: 書かれた is the past passive form of 書く: something was written, rather than doing the writing.

5.0.n: Together with の, this noun describes the kind of website.

5.1.n: の links ニュース to ホームページ to mean a website devoted to news.

5.2.n: ホームページ often means an entire website in Japanese, not just its front page.

5.3.n: を marks the websites as what the speaker looks at.

5.4.n: 見て is the linking て-form of 見る, connecting looking at the websites with the actions that follow.

6.0.n: 私 refers to the speaker, who immediately identifies themself as ニュース犬.

6.2.n: This is the speaker's character name or title, combining ニュース with 犬, meaning dog.

6.3.n: が marks 私、ニュース犬 as the person doing the thinking and speaking.

7.0.n: 思った is the plain past form of 思う and describes こと directly.

7.1.n: こと turns 思った into a noun phrase: the things the speaker thought.

7.2.n: を marks 思ったこと as the content the speaker will discuss.

7.3.n: This politely refers to the audience, now as the listeners rather than a direct greeting.

7.4.n: に marks the audience as the recipients of the speaker's words.

7.5.n: 話します is the polite form of 話す; here it announces what the speaker will do.

0.tip: こんばんは is a fixed greeting; its final は is pronounced わ.

1.lit: It is time for Easy Japanese News Wan.
1.tip: A program title followed by の時間です is a standard way to announce that it is starting.

2.lit: Everyone, it has been a long time.
2.tip: お久しぶりです is a polite greeting for meeting or addressing someone again after a while.

3.lit: As for this news, of NHK Web Easy and similar sites…
3.tip: The sentence continues across several subtitles, so this line is not a complete statement.

4.tip: The phrase ending in 書かれた describes the news websites mentioned in the next line.

5.tip: 見て links this action to what follows instead of ending the sentence.

6.tip: ニュース犬 identifies who 私 is; both refer to the same speaker.

7.lit: Will tell everyone what I thought.
7.tip: 思ったこと means what the speaker thought, with こと turning the preceding verb into a noun phrase.
